Promoting strength-ductility synergy by heterogeneous grain structure in a
zirconium-alloyed Fe-Mn-Al-C low-density steel
Yuheng Wang , Runze Yu , Fengchao An <sup>*</sup> , Suotao Wang <sup>**</sup>, Hao Wang , Zibo Zhao ,
Hongpu Yue , Tianxiang Gao , Junting Luo <sup>***</sup>, Junsong Zhang , Riping Liu
Center of Advanced Structured Materials, State Key Laboratory of Metastable Materials Science and Technology, Yanshan University, Qinhuangdao, 066004, China
A R T I C L E I N F O
Keywords:
Low-density steels
Bimodal grains
Zirconium addition
Mechanical properties
A B S T R A C T
Heterostructures, particularly dual-phase heterostructures, often lead to hetero-interfacial stress concentration,
and ultimately premature failure. though they benefit from heterogeneous deformation. Addressing the challenge
of strain localization and hetero-interfacial cracking, a single-phase heterogeneous grain structure is designed
through tuning zirconium (Zr) content and employing precise thermo-mechanical treatment. As Zr content in
creases to 0.50 wt %, a single-phase bimodal grain structure is successfully engineered, including soft coarse
grain zones (~5 μm in size and 65 % in area) and hard fine grain zones (~1 μm in size and 35 % in area). Such
bimodal heterostructure is mainly ascribed to the retarding effect of recrystallization, due to the drag effect of Zr
atoms and Zener pinning of ZrC. The synergistic effects of microstructural heterogeneity and ZrC precipitation
enhance the strengths. Furthermore, multistage deformation mechanisms, involving heterogeneous deformation-
induced hardening, dislocation slip and nanotwinning, enable the strain hardening capability and ductility.
1. Introduction
For structural alloys used in engineering applications, the simulta
neous enhancement of strength and ductility remains a critical chal
lenge. Recently, the Fe-Mn-Al-C-based steels have grained considerable
attention, due to the desirable strength-ductility synergy and lightness
[1–3]. To further enhance their mechanical properties, utilizing inco
herent B2 intermetallic compounds has been a vital approach through
addition of Ni [4,5]. However, such precipitation strengthening effect
usually leads to a significant enhancement of strengths accompanied by
a ductility loss, namely strength-ductility trade-off [6].
Recent development on alloys with heterostructues has a great po
tential to breakthrough such trade-off, thereby leading to various het
erostructures introduced by different approaches including muti-phase
structures [7,8], gradient grains [9], multi-modal grain structures [7–9].
For these heterostructures, the extra strengthening and hardening de
pends on the difference in hardness between the soft and hard regions,
which is usually referred as heterogeneous deformation-induced (HDI)
effect [7,8]. However, the pronounced disparity between soft and hard
zones (e.g., hardness and elastic modulus) often induces the interfacial
strain localization and premature failure, such as different dual-phase
systems including FCC/B2 dual-phase steels [10], and FCC/L2 me
dium entropy alloys [11,12]. In comparison to these dual-phase alloys,
heterogeneous grain structures usually exhibit hardness difference and
an identical elastic modulus between soft and hard zones [13,14], owing
to the single-phase structure. Such microstructural heterogeneities can
effective mitigate strain localization via reducing disparity between
hard and soft zones. Thus, introducing a single-phase heterogeneous
grain structure is a promising pathway to enhancing the strength and
ductility.
Following this line of thought, we introduce heterostructure grain
structure via a combination of thermo-mechanical treatment (TMT) and
addition of Zr. A typical single-phase heterostructure grain structure
including coarse grains and fine grains is successfully designed via
tuning Zr content. Such heterostructure effectively provides an extra
strengthening and hardening effect, thereby further enhancing the
strength and strain hardening capability.

2. Materials and methods
2.1. Material preparation
Three Fe-Mn-Al-C low density steels were melted using a vacuum
arc-melt furnace, and their chemical compositions are Fe-25Mn-7Al-
0.9C-0Zr. Fe-25Mn-7Al-0.9C-0.01Zr and Fe-25Mn-7Al-0.9C-0.50Zr
(wt. %), which are referred to as Zr0, Zr0.01 and Zr0.50 steels, respec
tively. For the melting process, the raw materials (>99.8 wt % pure)
were placed into the water-cooled copper crucible. Then, the furnace
was evacuated to a high vacuum level (the pressure below
bar) to
avoid gas contamination including oxygen (O), nitrogen (N) and
hydrogen (H). Additionally, introducing high-purity argon (Ar) into the

3.2. Tensile deformation behavior
Fig. 4a shows the engineering stress-strain curves of the Fe-Mn-Al-C
low density steels with different Zr content. In Zr0 steel, its yield
strength is ~435 MPa, the ultimate tensile strength is 820 MPa, and
fracture ductility is 52 %. As Zr content increased to 0.01 wt %, the
strengths of the Zr0.01 steel are slightly increased, i.e., yield strength:
~450 MPa, ultimate tensile strength: ~832 MPa, while its fracture
ductility is increased to 55 %. With further increasing of Zr content, the
Zr0.50 steel exhibits a reasonable strength-ductility combination, i.e.,
yield strength: ~505 MPa, ultimate tensile strength: ~855 MPa and
fracture ductility: 58 %. Similarly, a high true ultimate tensile strength
and true strain is observed in the Zr0.50 steel. This suggests that intro
ducing heterostructure in Fe-Mn-Al-C low-density steels through addi
tion of Zr can enhance the mechanical properties. The microscopic
fracture morphologies of these fractured Fe-Mn-Al-C low density steels
are shown in Fig. 4b–d. For the Zr0 steel, its facture surface is mainly
composed of small dimples and cleavage faces. As the Zr content
increasing, the dimples are obviously larger and deeper than those in Zr0
steel. and the density is also increased.

5. Conclusion
In present study, a single-phase heterogeneous grain structure, con
taining coarse grains with ~5 μm in size and 65 % in area and fine grains
with ~1 μm in size and 35 % in area, is successfully engineered in a Fe-
Mn-Al-C low density steel. As the Zr content increases to 0.50 wt %, the
drag effect of Zr atoms and Zener pinning of ZrC carbides is obvious
enhanced, which can retard the recrystallization process. Such retarding
recrystallization in turn assists the formation of bimodal grain structure.
The heterogeneous grain structure has yielded desirable enhancement in
strength-ductility synergy, in comparison to the Fe-Mn-Al-C steels
without Zr addition or with 0.01 wt % Zr addition. The significant
strengthening effect is mainly attributed to the grain boundary
strengthening, HDI strengthening and precipitation strengthening. For
the enhanced strain hardening capability and fracture ductility, the
deformation mechanisms are dominated by cooperating slip bands, HDI
hardening and deformation twins.

enhanced, which can retard the recrystallization process. Such retarding
recrystallization in turn assists the formation of bimodal grain structure.
The heterogeneous grain structure has yielded desirable enhancement in
strength-ductility synergy, in comparison to the Fe-Mn-Al-C steels
without Zr addition or with 0.01 wt % Zr addition. The significant
strengthening effect is mainly attributed to the grain boundary
strengthening, HDI strengthening and precipitation strengthening. For
the enhanced strain hardening capability and fracture ductility, the
deformation mechanisms are dominated by cooperating slip bands, HDI
hardening and deformation twins.
